clue.text: The place to find hipsters recycling their waste

indicators.note: recycling material turns it into something new, so these letters are worked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Trendy young people sorting out their rubbish for the recycling bins.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the fashionable spot where everything is happening, exactly where trendsetters gather.

clue.text: Deliver puppies, with assistance

parts.note: assistance is help

explanation.surface: A dog giving birth with a vet helping.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to whelp is to give birth, used of dogs and some other animals.

clue.text: Attempt to pronounce first letters of Swedish alphabet

indicators.note: to pronounce letters is to say their names out loud, so the result is spelt as it is spoken

parts.note: the first letters of the words Swedish and alphabet are S and A

explanation.surface: A learner trying to say the opening letters of the Swedish alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: S and A, spoken as letter names, sound like 'ess' and 'ay'.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay, as a verb or noun, is a try or endeavour, its older sense.

clue.text: French retailer rejected Formula 1 parts

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the whole thing is read in reverse
parts means splits open, so the one goes inside the formula

parts.note: a recipe is a formula for making something
the digit one looks like the letter I

explanation.surface: A French shop refusing to stock Formula 1 car parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formula 1' looks like motor racing. I goes into RECIPE, giving REICIPE, which reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An épicier is a French grocer, someone who sells provisions in a shop.

clue.text: Rows typically involve everyone rudely shouting at first

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Arguments usually draw in everybody shouting rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like quarrels, matching the shouting, but it means ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are rows or levels placed one above another, as in seating.

clue.text: A best man rollicking around hotel causes embarrassment

indicators.note: around puts the jumbled letters about the hotel letter
rollicking means boisterous, so the letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A rowdy best man at a hotel wedding reception causing awkwardness.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashment is the feeling of being ashamed or disconcerted, a close synonym.

clue.text: On the radio, music by The Specials and Cliff

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is only heard, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: The Specials were a British two-tone band who played ska, a Jamaican dance music

explanation.surface: A radio playlist pairing a Specials track with a Cliff Richard song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff' looks like Cliff Richard the singer, but it is the definition. In a non-rhotic British accent SKA and SCAR sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a steep rocky outcrop or crag, a word common in northern English place names.

clue.text: Something that's made to house mass burning

indicators.note: to house means to contain, so the made thing holds the mass letter

parts.note: a creation is something made
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A structure built to hold burning material in quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremation is the burning of a dead body, so it is a specific kind of burning.

clue.text: Roadie had worked for rock band

indicators.note: worked here means shaped or reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A roadie who used to work for a rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous English rock group from Oxford, known for OK Computer.

clue.text: Coins belonging to elderly people

definitions.meaning: ... means coins made of ...-coloured metal, loose change
... describes older people, as in ... surfers, from grey hair

explanation.surface: Pocket change owned by pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both coins and, as an adjective, relating to the older generation.

clue.text: Small space not entirely fit for a bathroom

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space, half an em

indicators.note: not entirely tells us to drop the last letter of the word for fit

parts.note: fit as in suitable means suited

explanation.surface: A cramped room that is not quite suitable to be turned into a bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An en suite is a private washroom attached directly to a bedroom, as in hotels.

clue.text: Liquorice flavouring agent is a requirement for a coating

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first two pieces serve as a coating, wrapped round the word is

parts.note: a requirement is a need
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone explaining that a sweet coating needs a liquorice-type flavouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a coating' reads as a layer on a sweet, but it says the first pieces coat the word is.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of the anise plant tastes of liquorice and is used to flavour sweets and drinks.

clue.text: Fitness tests disregarding the principles of all legitimate science

indicators.note: disregarding means leaving out, so the letters picked next are removed

parts.note: physicals are medical examinations checking fitness

indicators.note: principles here means first elements, so the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A sceptic dismissing fitness testing as ignoring the basic rules of real science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disregarding' removes A and L, the first letters of 'all legitimate', from PHYSICALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics is the natural science of matter, energy and motion.

clue.text: Try to bear a stupid person who's half-cut

parts.note: to bear, as in carry or hold, is to have

indicators.note: half-cut means cut in half, so only the first half of the word for a stupid person is kept

parts.note: a goon is a stupid person

explanation.surface: Putting up with a fool who is somewhat drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it halves GOON to GO.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go is the everyday idiom for making an attempt at something.

clue.text: Wacky baccy — free in a place frequented by surfers?

indicators.note: wacky means crazy, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A cannabis-friendly venue where beach surfers hang out, with weed given away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baccy' is British slang for tobacco; 'wacky baccy' is cannabis. The surfers are web surfers, not wave riders.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet cafe is where people go online, and browsing the web is called surfing.

clue.text: My rubbish mobile initially can't receive an unknown number

indicators.note: rubbish means useless, so the letters are treated as junk and rearranged
initially picks the first letter of each of the following words

parts.note: Y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A complaint that a useless phone won't take calls from an unrecognised number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British exclamations of surprise, like 'Gosh!'.

clue.text: A crime lab disposed of two bodies

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out differently, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A forensic lab getting rid of two corpses.
explanation.walkthrough: The bodies are legislative chambers, not corpses.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicameral parliament has two chambers, such as an upper and lower house.

clue.text: Seize absolute power before female does at the beginning

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: at the beginning picks only the opening letter of the preceding word

explanation.surface: Someone grabbing total control before a woman manages it.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprehend someone is to arrest or catch them, a synonym of seize.

clue.text: Lift provided by Wonderbra is excellent

indicators.note: provided by says the answer is supplied by the run of words that follows, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: An advert claiming a push-up bra gives superb uplift.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to elevate it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: To sum up, in retrospect: outside the Church Of England, there is equality

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the whole construction is read backwards
outside places the word for equality around the Church abbreviation

parts.note: par means equality, as in on a par
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A summary claiming that outside the established Church everyone is equal.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR outside CE gives PACER, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap is a brief summary, and to recap is to summarise briefly.

clue.text: Put down money - £25 — on a horse

parts.note: pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
a rider on a horse is up

explanation.surface: Betting twenty-five pounds on a horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: PONY is British slang for £25; a jockey riding is 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pony up is an idiom meaning to pay, especially reluctantly.

clue.text: Bird — outwardly bald — is perhaps covered in spots

indicators.note: outwardly says the word for bald sits on the outside, around the bird

parts.note: pated means having a pate, as in bald-pated
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird with a bald head whose plumage may be speckled.
explanation.walkthrough: Pated means having a pate (head), as in bald-pated; 'perhaps' marks spots as only one kind of decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a repeated decorative design, such as dots or stripes, is described this way.

clue.text: Famous British artist gets peanuts occasionally

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist

indicators.note: occasionally picks letters at regular gaps, here every second letter

explanation.surface: A well-known artist paid next to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means distinguished or celebrated, a synonym of famous.

clue.text: European newspaper is a failure and extremely divisive

parts.note: a lemon is a dud or failure

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: A critic calling a newspaper a flop that splits opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the leading French daily, published in Paris.

clue.text: Cocaine — with good joints — for someone who likes getting high?

parts.note: C is slang for cocaine
limber means supple, with joints moving freely

explanation.surface: Drugs and decent joints for someone who enjoys being high.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug-taking surface hides a mountaineer; 'joints' are body joints, not cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountaineer or rock climber literally enjoys reaching great heights.

clue.text: Boat toilet starts to overflow … eww!

parts.note: can is American slang for a toilet

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A boat's lavatory overflowing, to everyone's disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow boat paddled by hand.

clue.text: Born On The Fourth Of July upset servicemen very much

indicators.note: the fourth of picks the letter in fourth place of the next word
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, are servicemen

explanation.surface: Fans of the Oliver Stone war film being annoyed by military men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Born On The Fourth Of July' is the film title, but split up it gives B and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase intensifies a comparison, meaning by a great margin.

clue.text: London's oldest restaurant is the best!

definitions.meaning: ... in Covent Garden, founded in 1798, claims to be London's oldest restaurant
something that ... is excellent, in slang

explanation.surface: A diner praising a historic London restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the Covent Garden restaurant doubles as slang praise meaning tops.

clue.text: Name at the bottom of invite showing possible party venue

parts.note: a marque is a brand name, especially of a car

indicators.note: at the bottom of means the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A host's name signed at the foot of a party invitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tent put up for weddings and garden parties can host a celebration.

clue.text: Dancing nude almost felt necessary

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so they land in a new order
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone who felt it was almost essential to dance naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful is a slightly old-fashioned word for required or essential.

clue.text: Where you might see stray cats running around letting out a scream

indicators.note: letting out means releasing, so the letter a is removed
running around signals turning the place for stray cats back to front

parts.words: Where you might see stray cats
parts.note: alley cats are strays, so an alley is where they roam

explanation.surface: Stray cats tearing round a back street, one of them screeching.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLEY backwards is YELLA; 'letting out a' removes the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A yell is a loud cry, the same sense as a scream used as a noun.

clue.text: Exciting events in the run up to Christmas sure getting messy

parts.note: Advent is the church season of the four weeks before Christmas

indicators.note: getting messy means becoming jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pre-Christmas excitement that is sure to turn chaotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventures are thrilling or daring experiences, so the plural matches exciting events.
